scope: Delivery that ships XeniaCore (docs/xenios-playlist.md), chained after the Xbox 360 playlist review, whose engine_binaries_bundled is empty. It binds the engine pin (build-utils/xenia/core-pin.json: XeniOS revision, binary, packaged fingerprint, producing run), the RewindBox files compiled into that binary, and the two statically linked LGPL libraries of XeniOS, FFmpeg and libmspack: their exact sources, configuration and the relinking means chosen. Apple's Metal Shader Converter runtime ships beside it, not built from source, under Apple's EA1844 (assets/legal/metal-shader-converter; open points 1-3 of the maintainer's dossier stay open). No package, dependency or source declaration changes. This review does not attest complete corresponding source and is not a legal clearance.

engine.recipe_note: These RewindBox files are compiled into, or drive the build of, the pinned binary; the collector refuses the tree if any of them differs, so the IPA's own host source archive (BUILD_SOURCE_EVIDENCE.json immutable_host_source_archive) holds the recipe that built it.
engine.unpinned_build_inputs: xenia-build.py fetchdata downloads the embedded game databases (xenia-manager/x360db, the xenia-canary game-compatibility release) at build time without a pinned revision; a later rebuild may embed newer data. They are data, not LGPL code.

lgpl_components.name: FFmpeg
lgpl_components.license_evidence: third_party/ffmpeg-xenia/config.h of the pinned revision: FFMPEG_LICENSE "LGPL version 2.1 or later", FFMPEG_CONFIGURATION "xenia-custom"; no CONFIG_GPL, CONFIG_NONFREE or CONFIG_VERSION3 define in the overlay. The LGPL-2.1 text ships in the XeniOS acknowledgements. The 13 libswresample files compiled, and the templates they include, carry FFmpeg's LGPL 2.1-or-later header at the pinned gitlink (read 14 Nov 2026).

configuration.build: third_party/CMakeLists.txt of the pinned revision lists 146 FFmpeg source files (13 of them architecture-specific: 11 aarch64, 2 x86) for the four static libraries; libswresample (13 of them, added upstream after cf7c7ee45, used by the XMP player of xenia-apu) is new in XeniOS 2.3.2; FFmpeg's configure is not run

lgpl_components.modifications_note: A fork (branch xmaframes, which adds the xmaframes decoder); its changes from upstream FFmpeg were not reviewed here. The pinned gitlink is the exact source.

lgpl_components.name: libmspack
lgpl_components.license_evidence: lzxd.c header (GNU LGPL version 2.1, (C) 2003-2013 Stuart Caie) and COPYING.LIB (blob b1e3f5a2638797271cbc9b91b856c05ed6942c8f) in the pinned revision; the text ships in the XeniOS acknowledgements.

configuration.build: third_party/CMakeLists.txt: static library mspack from lzxd.c, system.c and logging.cc

lgpl_components.modifications_note: A vendored subset (the LZX decoder); logging.cc is Xenia's own. Its differences from an upstream libmspack release were not reviewed here.

other_components.Boost.Context: BSL-1.0, not LGPL: make_, jump_ and ontop_arm64_aapcs_macho_gas.S of boostorg/context at d2142b69252150dafb5f6569b7eb9a42312a92a3 (assets/legal/xenios/license-sources.json provenance)
other_components.Metal Shader Converter: Apple binary, Frameworks/libmetalirconverter.dylib, bytes unchanged except the code signature; no source exists to offer (build-utils/xenia/source.json shader_converter)

relinking_means.statement: The complete source of XeniaCore (XeniOS at the pinned revision with its submodules, FFmpeg at the pinned gitlink, libmspack in-tree) and the scripts that build it (the recipe files bound above, in the IPA's immutable host source archive) let a user rebuild XeniaCore.framework with a modified FFmpeg or libmspack and place it back in the app. This is the means chosen, not a statement that it satisfies the licence.
relinking_means.open: The sources are referenced by immutable revision and URL, not copied into the IPA. Whether that is the 'accompany' of 6(a) or calls for 6(c)/(d) (a written offer, or equivalent access from the same place) is the maintainer's decision; it is not settled here. Rebuilding also needs Apple's iOS SDK and the converter runtime, and re-signing the app; this review does not change that.
